title: Boss: the resilient client
summary: Call several services at once, give up on slow ones, retry flaky ones, and keep the number of parallel calls under control.

steps.title: One new tool: SemaphoreSlim
body: Real services fail, stall and rate-limit you. The four challenges below build the helpers that every API client ends up needing. The last one needs a tool you have not met yet.
A **`SemaphoreSlim`** is a counter of free slots. It lets at most *N* pieces of code through at a time.
await gate.WaitAsync();            // take a slot; waits (without blocking) if none is free
gate.Release();                // give the slot back, even if the work failed
Start a hundred tasks that all do this, and only two are ever inside the `try` at once. The `finally` matters: a slot that is never released is lost for good.

steps.title: Three services, one wait
prompt: A dashboard needs data from three services. The tests provide them; each takes about 30 ms:
```csharp
static class Services
public static Task<string> GetNameAsync(int userId);
public static Task<int> GetOrderCountAsync(int userId);
public static Task<int> GetBalanceAsync(int userId);
Write `static async Task<string> BuildDashboardAsync(int userId)`. It returns text like:
```text
Maya: 3 orders, balance 120
All three calls must be **in progress at the same time**, so the whole thing takes about 30 ms, not 90.
starter: // the other two calls are missing, and awaiting one by one is too slow
solution: return $"{await nameTask}: {await ordersTask} orders, balance {await balanceTask}";
template: Dojo.Eq("all 3 service calls were in progress at the same time", 3, Services.MaxInFlight);
Dojo.Eq("each service was called once", 3, Services.Calls);
public static Task<string> GetNameAsync(int userId) => Slow(userId == 1 ? "Maya" : "Omar");
public static Task<int> GetOrderCountAsync(int userId) => Slow(userId == 1 ? 3 : 1);
public static Task<int> GetBalanceAsync(int userId) => Slow(userId == 1 ? 120 : 40);
hints: Call all three methods first and keep the three tasks in variables. Do not `await` anything until all three have been started.
The tasks have different result types, so `Task.WhenAll` cannot hand you one array. Use `await Task.WhenAll(nameTask, ordersTask, balanceTask);` only to wait.
After that, `await nameTask`, `await ordersTask` and `await balanceTask` each return at once with the value. Build the string from those.

steps.title: A timeout wrapper
prompt: Some calls hang. Write a generic helper that waits for a task, but only for so long:
```csharp
static async Task<T> WithTimeoutAsync<T>(Task<T> task, int timeoutMs, T fallback)
- If `task` finishes within `timeoutMs` milliseconds, return its result.
- If it does not, return `fallback`.
- If `task` **fails** with its own exception, that exception must still reach the caller. Only a timeout is turned into the fallback.
```csharp
int stock = await WithTimeoutAsync(GetStockAsync("TEA"), 200, -1);
You are given a task, not a token, so this is a job for `WaitAsync`.
starter: static async Task<T> WithTimeoutAsync<T>(Task<T> task, int timeoutMs, T fallback)
// this waits for ever if the task never finishes
solution: static async Task<T> WithTimeoutAsync<T>(Task<T> task, int timeoutMs, T fallback)
template: static async Task<T> After<T>(int ms, T value) { await Task.Delay(ms); return value; }
static async Task<int> Broken() { await Task.Delay(5); throw new InvalidOperationException("service down"); }
Dojo.Eq("a task that finishes in time gives its own result", 12, await WithTimeoutAsync(After(5, 12), 3000, -1));
Dojo.Eq("it works for strings too", "fresh", await WithTimeoutAsync(After(5, "fresh"), 3000, "cached"));
Dojo.Check("a task that never finishes does not hang the caller", first == guarded, "WithTimeoutAsync was still waiting long after the 20 ms timeout");
if (first == guarded) Dojo.Eq("and the fallback is returned", -1, await guarded);
Dojo.Eq("a failing task still throws its own exception", "InvalidOperationException", outcome);
hints: `task.WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(timeoutMs))` is a task that fails with `TimeoutException` when the time runs out. Await that instead of `task`.
Wrap the `await` in `try` and add `catch (TimeoutException) { return fallback; }`.
Catch **only** `TimeoutException`. A `catch (Exception)` would also swallow the task's own failure, which must get through.

steps.title: Retry with backoff
prompt: A flaky service often works on the second or third try. Hammering it straight away makes things worse, so each retry waits **twice as long** as the one before. That is called exponential backoff.
```csharp
static async Task<T> RetryAsync<T>(
Func<Task<T>> action, int maxAttempts, int baseDelayMs, Func<int, Task> delay)
- Call `action()` and await it. If it succeeds, return the result.

- If it throws and attempts remain, wait and try again. Wait by calling `await delay(ms)` with `baseDelayMs` after the 1st failure, `2 * baseDelayMs` after the 2nd, `4 * baseDelayMs` after the 3rd, and so on.
- If attempt number `maxAttempts` also throws, let that exception through. Do not wait after the final failure.
`delay` is passed in so the tests can record the waits without really waiting. In production you would pass `ms => Task.Delay(ms)`.
With `maxAttempts` 4 and `baseDelayMs` 10, an action that fails twice and then works causes waits of 10 and 20.
starter: Func<Task<T>> action, int maxAttempts, int baseDelayMs, Func<int, Task> delay)
solution: Func<Task<T>> action, int maxAttempts, int baseDelayMs, Func<int, Task> delay)
template: Func<int, Task> record = ms => { waits.Add(ms); return Task.CompletedTask; };
if (attempts <= failures) throw new InvalidOperationException("attempt " + attempts + " failed");
Dojo.Eq("an action that works first time is called once", "ok after 1", await RetryAsync(failing(0), 4, 10, record));
Dojo.Eq("and there was no waiting", 0, waits.Count);
Dojo.Eq("an action that fails twice succeeds on attempt 3", "ok after 3", await RetryAsync(failing(2), 4, 10, record));
Dojo.Eq("the waits were 10 then 20", new List<int> { 10, 20 }, waits);
Dojo.Eq("after maxAttempts failures the last exception gets through", "attempt 4 failed", outcome);
Dojo.Eq("the action was tried exactly 4 times", 4, attempts);
Dojo.Eq("the waits were 5, 10, 20, with none after the final failure", new List<int> { 5, 10, 20 }, waits);
Dojo.Eq("maxAttempts 1 means no retries at all", "attempt 1 failed", outcome);
hints: Use a loop that counts attempts from 1. Inside it, `try { return await action(); }`. A successful attempt leaves the method through that `return`.
In the `catch`, decide: if this was attempt number `maxAttempts`, rethrow with `throw;`. Otherwise fall out of the `catch` and continue.
Keep an `int wait = baseDelayMs;`. After a failed attempt that is not the last: `await delay(wait); wait *= 2;` and go round again.

steps.title: Retry and a limit, for Sidekick
prompt: **Sidekick piece: the resilient client.** `sk links` fetches many pages at once, but at most 4 at a time, and it retries a flaky site. Here are the two helpers it uses. They are generic, so anything in Sidekick can use them.
1. `static async Task<T> Retry<T>(Func<Task<T>> action, int attempts, Func<int, Task> wait)`
- `attempts` below 1 throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.

- Await `action()`. On success return the value. When it throws and this was not the last attempt, `await wait(attemptNumber)` (1 after the first failure, 2 after the second ...) and try again. The caller decides the backoff: `sk` passes `attempt => Task.Delay(200 * attempt)`.
- The last failure's exception reaches the caller; no wait after it.
2. `static async Task<List<TResult>> ForEachLimited<T, TResult>(IReadOnlyList<T> items, int limit, Func<T, Task<TResult>> work)`
- `limit` below 1 throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.
- Run `work` for every item with **at most** `limit` running at once (use a `SemaphoreSlim`), and return the results in the order of `items`.
```csharp
await ForEachLimited(urls, 4, url => Retry(() => fetch(url), 3, a => Task.Delay(200 * a)));

foreach (var item in items) results.Add(await work(item));

require.message: Limits the work with a SemaphoreSlim
Releases the slot in a finally block

hints: Retry: `for (int attempt = 1; ; attempt++) { try { return await action(); } catch (Exception) when (attempt < attempts) { await wait(attempt); } }`. The filter lets the last failure escape.
ForEachLimited: `using var gate = new SemaphoreSlim(limit);` and start one task per item: `await gate.WaitAsync(); try { return await work(item); } finally { gate.Release(); }`.
Collect them with `items.Select(async item => ...).ToList()` and `return (await Task.WhenAll(running)).ToList();`.
